column2: A module/class should have one reason to change.
Subtypes must be usable anywhere the base type is expected without breaking correctness.
High-level modules depend on abstractions, not concrete low-level details.
Composition uses has-a relationships; inheritance uses is-a subclassing.
Fat interfaces that force clients to depend on unused methods.
Extend via new implementations/strategies without modifying existing core code.
Multiple classes implementing the same interface method differently.
It acts like hidden global mutable state and hurts testing.
Encapsulation hides internals; abstraction models essential interfaces/concepts.
